name: comp-379

frames.best_why: Menu is open with icon tiles and two-line descriptions, and the Heading 1 row is highlighted.

tagline: A plus button opens a menu of block types, each with an icon and a short hint.
summary: A plus button beside a document title opens a menu for adding content. Five rows pair a bordered icon tile with a block type and a one-line description: text, quote, divider and two headings.
appearance: A rounded dark card shows 'Untitled document' and a grey hint, with a round ghost plus button at the right. The open menu drops below: a small 'Add block' label, then five rows, each starting with a tiny bordered icon square and holding a bold type name over a faint description.
behaviour: Clicking the plus opens the menu; hovering a row highlights it and choosing one closes the menu. The document does not change in this demo.
demo_content: Card 'Untitled document' with 'Add a block to keep writing'; menu has Text, Quote, Divider, Heading 1 and Heading 2.
search_phrases: menu to add text quote or heading
insert content blocks from a dropdown
editor add block menu with icons
choose a text or heading block
use_when: An editor needs a compact menu for inserting new content blocks by type.
avoid_when: Rows are packed into a narrow menu, so descriptions wrap and the icons crowd the text.
customise: The five block options, icons and descriptions are written in the file; wiring them to an editor means adding handlers.
weight_why: A small menu of five rows with static icons; nothing runs in the background.

a11y.note: The plus has an aria-label and rows use menu semantics; icon tiles are hidden from screen readers while titles carry meaning.

issues: The menu is narrow, so block descriptions wrap into cramped two-line rows.
Block choices are not wired to any editor action in the demo.
polish_why: Clear icon-plus-label rows; the cramped narrow menu and wrapped hints hold it back.
title: Content Block Picker
